cls: Thiazolidinedione (TZD) PPAR-gamma agonist; oral antidiabetic insulin sensitizer
pharm: Activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-gamma), with partial PPAR-alpha activity, increasing peripheral insulin sensitivity and reducing hepatic glucose output to improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.
quick: Not recommended; insulin preferred in pregnancy
No specific dose adjustment; use caution with fluid retention
Monitor LFTs; avoid in active liver disease or ALT >2.5x ULN
Limit; may worsen glycemic control and liver risk
HbA1c, liver enzymes, weight, edema, signs of heart failure
summary: Lobeglitazone is a thiazolidinedione (TZD) PPAR-gamma agonist (with partial PPAR-alpha activity) used as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, given as a low oral dose of 0.5 mg once daily. As an insulin sensitizer it shares the TZD class effects and risks of pioglitazone and rosiglitazone, including fluid retention and edema, weight gain, an increased risk of bone fractures (particularly in women), a possible class-related bladder cancer signal, and the potential to precipitate or worsen heart failure. It is marketed outside the United States (e.g., South Korea under the brand Duvie, and India) and is NOT FDA-approved. Used alone it has a low risk of hypoglycemia, which increases when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea.
indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
May be used as monotherapy or in combination with other oral antidiabetic agents (e.g., metformin) or insulin per local labeling

dosage.n: Taken with or without food; fixed dose (no routine titration)

dosage.d: 0.5 mg once daily added to existing therapy
dosage.n: Reduce insulin/sulfonylurea dose if hypoglycemia occurs

dosage.d: Do not initiate in NYHA Class III-IV heart failure; discontinue if heart failure develops or worsens
dosage.n: Class effect - TZDs cause fluid retention

admin: Take one 0.5 mg tablet once daily, at approximately the same time each day
May be taken with or without food
Continue diet, exercise, and other antidiabetic measures as prescribed
Glycemic effect develops gradually over weeks; do not expect an immediate response
If used with insulin or a sulfonylurea, watch for hypoglycemia and adjust those agents as needed
moa: Lobeglitazone is a thiazolidinedione that acts as a potent agonist of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-gamma), with additional partial PPAR-alpha activity. Activation of PPAR-gamma in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and liver modulates transcription of genes involved in glucose and lipid metabolism, enhancing peripheral insulin sensitivity, promoting glucose uptake, and decreasing hepatic glucose production. Its effect requires the presence of insulin and develops gradually over several weeks. The partial PPAR-alpha activity may contribute to favorable effects on lipids. Because it does not stimulate insulin secretion, it does not cause hypoglycemia when used as monotherapy.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to lobeglitazone or any component of the formulation
NYHA Class III or IV heart failure
Diabetic ketoacidosis or type 1 diabetes mellitus
Active liver disease or significant hepatic impairment
relative: History of heart failure or risk of fluid overload (NYHA Class I-II - use with caution)
Pre-existing edema or concurrent use of agents that cause fluid retention (e.g., insulin, NSAIDs)
Active or history of bladder cancer, or unexplained macroscopic hematuria (TZD class signal)
Osteoporosis or high fracture risk, particularly in postmenopausal women
Baseline liver enzyme elevation (ALT > 2.5x upper limit of normal)
monitor: Liver function tests (ALT) at baseline and periodically
Signs and symptoms of heart failure (dyspnea, edema, rapid weight gain)

preg: There are no adequate, well-controlled data in pregnant women, and thiazolidinediones are generally not recommended during pregnancy. Insulin is preferred to maintain glycemic control in pregnancy. Use lobeglitazone in pregnancy only if the potential benefit clearly justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether lobeglitazone is excreted in human milk; thiazolidinediones have been detected in the milk of lactating animals. Because of the potential for adverse effects in the breastfed infant, avoid use during breastfeeding or discontinue nursing.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is generally required for renal impairment. Use with caution because of the risk of fluid retention and edema, and avoid in patients with significant volume overload. Avoid use in patients with diabetic ketoacidosis.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease and in patients with ALT greater than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. As a thiazolidinedione, hepatic monitoring is advised: check liver enzymes before starting therapy and periodically thereafter. Discontinue if ALT rises to more than 3 times the upper limit of normal or if jaundice or symptoms of hepatic injury occur.

major: Insulin - increased risk of fluid retention, edema, heart failure, and hypoglycemia; consider reducing insulin dose
Sulfonylureas - additive glucose lowering and increased hypoglycemia risk; reduce sulfonylurea dose if needed
moderate: NSAIDs - additive fluid retention and edema
Gemfibrozil and other strong CYP2C8/CYP3A4 inhibitors - may increase lobeglitazone exposure (TZD class metabolized via CYP enzymes)
Rifampin and other CYP inducers - may reduce lobeglitazone exposure and efficacy
Drugs causing hyperglycemia (corticosteroids, thiazides, estrogens, sympathomimetics) - may reduce glycemic control
minor: Other oral antidiabetic agents (e.g., metformin) - additive glucose-lowering effect
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food interaction reported.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol intake; it can impair glycemic control and may add to hepatic risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause small decreases in hemoglobin and hematocrit (hemodilution from fluid retention) and elevations in liver enzymes; monitor accordingly.

serious: Congestive heart failure / worsening of heart failure
Hypoglycemia when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
rare: Bladder cancer (possible class-related signal with thiazolidinediones)
emergency: Acute decompensated heart failure / pulmonary edema

monitoring: HbA1c approximately every 3 months and fasting plasma glucose
Liver function tests (ALT) at baseline and periodically
Body weight and signs of fluid retention/edema
Symptoms and signs of heart failure (dyspnea, edema, rapid weight gain)
Periodic eye examination if visual symptoms (macular edema)
counsel: Take one tablet once daily; the full blood-sugar benefit builds up over several weeks
Tell your doctor promptly about rapid weight gain, swelling of the legs/ankles, or shortness of breath - these can be signs of fluid buildup or heart failure
This class of medicine can increase the risk of broken bones, especially in women; discuss bone health
Report any blood in the urine, painful or urgent urination promptly
If you also take insulin or a sulfonylurea, know the signs of low blood sugar and how to treat it
Keep regular appointments for blood sugar and liver blood tests; report yellowing of the skin/eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness
pk: Gradual; glycemic effect develops over several weeks
Plasma concentration peaks roughly 1-2 hours after an oral dose
Effect sustained over 24 hours; dosed once daily
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light, per local labeling
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; used outside the United States (e.g., South Korea under the brand Duvie, and India) - record is based on the Korean MFDS/Indian regulatory label and published prescribing information
Effective at a notably low oral dose (0.5 mg once daily), reflecting high PPAR-gamma potency
Shares the thiazolidinedione class risks of pioglitazone/rosiglitazone: fluid retention/edema, weight gain, heart failure, bone fractures, and a possible bladder cancer signal
Do not initiate in NYHA Class III-IV heart failure; discontinue if heart failure develops or worsens
Hepatic monitoring is recommended (TZD class); check liver enzymes at baseline and periodically
Low hypoglycemia risk as monotherapy; risk rises when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. As with other thiazolidinediones, overdose is not expected to cause hypoglycemia unless taken with insulin or a sulfonylurea, but may exaggerate class effects such as fluid retention and edema. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive and symptomatic care, monitoring for heart failure and hypoglycemia, and treat hypoglycemia with glucose as needed.
